page: Amazon Web Services r5d.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores with 2 threads per core) powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro System, the instance is allocated 768 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. Local storage consists of 3,600 GB of NVMe SSD instance storage. Networking provides a baseline bandwidth of 25 Gbps. The instance contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark data displays high throughput across parallel and memory-intensive metrics alongside moderate single-thread efficiency. The instance achieved 81,326.61 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a PassMark CPU score of 55,799.92, placing both in the top tier. Uncached memory read bandwidth reached 219.97 GB/sec, supporting strong database operations (21,671.55 on PassMark) and 77.77 million Redis SET operations per second. Conversely, single-core stress-ng (1,385.79) and single-threaded gzip compression (23.34 GB/sec) scored in the bottom quartile, reflecting modest per-thread execution speed.

Without dedicated GPU accelerators, the instance demonstrates limited capability for deep learning generation workloads, achieving 5.49 tokens per second for text generation on a 7B model. However, its balanced combination of 768 GB of RAM, integrated 3.6 TB NVMe storage, and 25 Gbps networking offers high resource density for scale-up relational databases, in-memory caching platforms, and intensive data processing pipelines that do not depend on accelerated compute.
description: Amazon Web Services r5d.24xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro instance equipped with 96 vCPUs across 48 physical Intel Xeon 8259CL cores at 3.1 GHz, 768 GB of DDR4 RAM, and 3,600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It provides 25 Gbps baseline networking and operates without GPU accelerators. The instance delivers top-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth, reaching 77.77 million Redis SET operations per second and high PassMark database ratings. Its per-core single-threaded benchmarks and language model generation speeds fall into lower performance bands. The instance profile is suited for memory-intensive, I/O-heavy workloads including distributed caching tiers, in-memory databases, and large relational database servers requiring fast local ephemeral storage.
